commit: HEAD of the branch (see git log)

requirements.notes: Measured locally: semantic_participants 8 (all eight admitted participants acted; 129 actions in a 33-module open_digital world with 196 tools, 24 rounds). The world is a 4.0 family, not the v5 standard population profile (workstream B not merged).
Measured: model_weight_copies 1, participants_sharing_weights 8 (same weights object and embedding storage).

Measured: tool_selection_accuracy 0.6083 (73/120, 95% CI 0.519-0.691) on held-out situations from 12 unseen templates, 10 options; p vs random 4.4e-42; random 0.10, BM25 0.167. Passes the 0.6 threshold by a small margin; the interval's lower bound is below 0.6.
Measured: comprehension_accuracy 0.900 (CI 0.833-0.942), p vs chance 3.3e-51, unseen genres 0.817.
Measured: consequential_actions_executed 15 (4 participants), counted from the event log.

Measured: verified_productive_results 2 (a 2,500-cent payment owed between participants, verified from ledger postings; a rented cloud instance, verified from the instances table). No document, program or question-and-answer exchange was verified.

Measured: peak VRAM 5,813 MiB, 252 GPU tokens/s, 8.9 rows per batch, 200,616 prompt tokens from the prefix cache, CPU 6.5 tokens/s (fp32, 4 threads); prefix-cache speedup 1.00 on eight argument prompts.
Measured: semantic_model_params 596,049,920 (Qwen3-0.6B); smaller_alternatives_benchmarked 2 (SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M) in the gate test, plus two trained heads (2.1M, 23.1M) in SP-3.2b.

Measured: model_sizes_compared 6 (2.1M n-gram head, 23.1M MiniLM+head, SmolLM2-135M, SmolLM2-360M, Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B), capabilities_benchmarked 8. Smallest effective (all test items / unseen templates): content Qwen3-0.6B / Qwen3-0.6B; situation n-gram head / Qwen3-1.7B; tool choice Qwen3-0.6B; communication SmolLM2-135M; incentives n-gram head / Qwen3-1.7B; negotiation Qwen3-1.7B / none; programming Qwen3-1.7B; strategy Qwen3-1.7B / Qwen3-1.7B.

limitations: Participants are weak agents: in the Gate H run 74 of 129 calls were rejected and 2 of 8 goals were met; no document, program or two-sided exchange by Qwen3-0.6B.
Gate H runs in the 4.0 open_digital world family; the v5 standard population (workstream B) is not merged.
H.4 passes by a small margin (0.608, CI lower bound 0.519).
Thinking mode makes each tool choice cost about 380 generated tokens; decoding is a plain PyTorch loop (no CUDA graphs or paged KV cache).
The prefix cache saves prefill only; with a 150-token shared system prompt it did not change wall time; in bfloat16 it can change greedy outputs (5 of 8 identical).
int8 dynamic quantization is CPU only and was not benchmarked for quality; no GPU quantization kernel is available in the environment.
Evaluation sets are template-generated from world situations; communication is checked automatically, not by a reader.
integration_notes: semantic/modules.py imports semantic/recording.py (kernel module semantic_inference, host admin). If D1 also creates semantic/modules.py, keep both import lines.
Worlds that host semantic participants add the module with extra_modules=['semantic_inference'].
SemanticService needs max_new_tokens >= think_tokens + arg_tokens of its participants (640 for the defaults); SemanticGroup.participant raises otherwise.
Benchmark weights (1.09 GB) were downloaded to the shared HF cache: SmolLM2-135M-Instruct, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct, all-MiniLM-L6-v2. No package was installed.
Gate H takes about 13 minutes (7 GB GPU, 4 CPUs); SP-3.2b about 40 minutes (10 GB GPU, 2 CPUs).
The participant parameters most likely to matter for v5 domains: SemanticParticipant.choice_method, think_tokens, arg_mode, n_candidates, context_chars.
